prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and quantum spin Hall effect, and for the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B038 as my preferred prize and I have not changed configuration since round 1. Having heard the whole exchange, the case rests on one chain that I can state in a sentence: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling gives a graphene-like model a Z2 invariant and a protected helical edge, and Molenkamp's group observed that edge conduction in HgTe wells in 2007, after which independent groups confirmed it in several material families by transport and ARPES. That is a clue from nature answering a theoretical prediction, which is the thing I look for. On the chair's overlap question, the 2016 prize rewarded topological phase transitions and the integer quantum Hall plateau, which are protected by broken time reversal and a Chern number. The time-reversal-invariant Z2 class is a different symmetry class, a different invariant and a different experimental signature, so I can write that distinction into a citation. I would keep the citation narrow to the quantum spin Hall state and the topological insulator concept, and leave the 3D materials work visibly outside the credit rather than pretending the three names cover it.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the weak point and I will not hide it. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe quantum-well realisation that told Molenkamp where to look, Zhang is deceased, and the 3D work of Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents and Hasan is a further claimant, so a three-name list leaves a visible gap. The experimental half also rests on essentially one group for the first observation. B046 has a cleaner credit and a longer, more varied record of independent reproduction, and if the expert reports on Kane-Mele versus BHZ priority came back unfavourably, I would accept that B046 is the safer prize. The 2016 overlap is answerable but a sceptic will still raise it.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks are a new way of observing nature, Katori-Ye is the cleanest credit, and the 2005 overlap is a factual question that must be settled first.
responses.response: Stefan, you have settled the 2005 point for us, and I should withdraw the argument I made against B046 in round 1. The 2005 prize went to Glauber, Hall and Hansch; Ye was Hall's postdoc and not a laureate, so I was wrong to say he already shares it. That removes the weakest part of my reservation. What remains is the distinction of kind: the fundamental-physics results so far (constants, dark matter, redshift over millimetres) are limits and demonstrations, not findings, and the SI redefinition has not happened. I do not think that is a reason to rank it below B038 on rigour. I still weigh a verified new state of matter slightly above a record in precision, so my preference stays, but I would defend B046 in the vote without difficulty if the committee prefers it. Your recusal question is for the Chair, but I would say that a declared proximity to Ye is a good reason for you to step back from the final decision on B046.

responses.point: B038 needs an expert account of Kane-Mele versus BHZ priority, and the citation should rest on the Z2 prediction and the first observation, with the gap stated openly.
responses.response: Eva, I agree and I would go a step further than my round-1 request. As Secretary I would want the outside experts to be asked three specific questions: whether Kane and Mele's Z2 classification and edge-state argument stands independently of BHZ; whether BHZ's contribution is the material-specific proposal and not the concept; and whether the 3D topological insulator work is a separate discovery that the committee should explicitly exclude. If the answer to the first is yes and to the second is that the proposal sharpened a measurement but did not create the concept, then a citation limited to the 2D quantum spin Hall state is defensible with Molenkamp, in the way the committee has defended experimental-plus-theory trios before. I accept your point that one experimental group is the thinner half, and I would treat that as the main residual risk, not the Zhang question.

responses.point: The Z2 class is distinct from what was honoured in 2016 and the chain from prediction to measurement is complete and confirmed for over fifteen years.
responses.response: Olle, I agree with your main reading and I want to answer the chair's question on the 2016 overlap in terms we can use. Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz were honoured for topological phase transitions and the topological explanation of the quantised Hall conductance, where the invariant is a Chern number and time reversal is broken. Kane and Mele's insulator is protected by time-reversal symmetry and carries a Z2 invariant, and its edge channels come in counter-propagating spin-momentum-locked pairs with no net magnetic field. I would write that into the citation by naming time-reversal invariance explicitly. Where I differ from you slightly is on width: I would not let the citation drift to the broader topological-materials program, because that would invite exactly the credit gap on 3D materials and BHZ that you and Eva flag.

responses.point: B046 is the only candidate that five of eight members placed in their top three, from members with quite different tastes, and the credit can be defended without a long attribution argument.
responses.response: Mark, I take the breadth of support seriously, and you are right that it comes from people with different tastes, which is a stronger signal than five like-minded votes. But I do not treat a count as a scientific judgment, and I would point out that the three members behind B038 are the three condensed-matter-minded members who can assess its claim in detail, while the lattice-clock members are the ones who know that field best. So the split looks like expertise speaking in both directions and not a reason to defer. Your reservation on IceCube is one I share, and I think you were right to move away from a one-name prize on a collaboration of hundreds. On B046 I would now say my objection is only about discovery versus instrument, and I do not regard it as disqualifying.

responses.point: The lattice clock is a discovery-type result in atomic physics because theory and experiment agree quantitatively, and it is distinct from the comb and the single-ion prizes as a way of interrogating many atoms at once.
responses.response: Eva, your account is persuasive on the physics: magic-wavelength trapping, quantitative control of blackbody and hyperfine shifts, and reproduction across JILA, RIKEN, PTB, NIST and SYRTE is a mature, confirmed result and not an extrapolation. I accept your distinction from the comb and from the single-ion work. Our disagreement is then narrow. You apply the discovery-versus-instrument test and find the clock on the discovery side; I apply the same test and find that the strongest discovery content, a new state of matter, sits with B038, while the clock's discoveries about constants and dark matter are still ahead of it. I would ask the committee to write a citation for B046 that names the magic-wavelength lattice and its realisation, not the comb or the SI redefinition, if it goes that way.

uncertainties: Whether outside experts will confirm that Kane-Mele is independent of the BHZ proposal, which decides whether three names without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang can be defended.
Whether the committee accepts the Z2 time-reversal-invariant class as distinct from the 2016 prize and whether the citation wording can carry that distinction.
Whether the lattice-clock fundamental-physics payoff will become findings rather than limits, and whether the SI redefinition changes the maturity argument.
Whether my preference for a new-matter discovery over a precision instrument is a stable principle or a taste of mine, since the colleagues who know metrology best rank B046 first.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted name. My collaborator Thomas Van Riet and my supervisor David Gross have no link to B038, B046 or B051. I note that I proposed B051 (WMAP) at opening, which is a scientific preference and not a personal tie. I have no connection to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Katori or Ye.
